teams.name: DINO NUGGETS

nameHistory.name: The Man the Myth the Legend

teams.commentary: A month ago Baker hadn't made a single roster move. Now he's in first place, and the move he finally made is why. The Brewers just went up two games to none on the Dodgers in the NLCS, and Baker's B-grade draft just passed the A-plus Cartel, so the small-market energy is going around. With Chuba Hubbard on a Panthers bye, MarShawn Lloyd, picked up a week ago, started and scored 16, Jahmyr Gibbs went for 35, Justin Jefferson came back with 16, and the Dino Nuggets beat Foy by more than 36. The lineup still has a tight end problem: Harold Fannin Jr., an $18 keeper, scored 0.9 while Hunter Henry scored 11.9 on the bench, and Dallas Goedert no longer carries an injury tag, which means Baker now has three tight ends and no idea which one to start. The committee would also like to note that Rico Dowdle is still out and the next back behind Gibbs and Hubbard projects around 2 a game. First place looks good on the Dino Nuggets, and the second-softest remaining schedule in the league says they could stay a while.

teams.name: Cachasol Cartel

nameHistory.name: C u M C back KIDZ!!!

teams.commentary: Mike D. once named his team Switch Hitters, and he has never stopped believing in the bit. This week he owned three quarterbacks and switched to the wrong one: Jayden Daniels scored 32.1 on the bench in a game Washington still managed to lose after leading by 14 in the fourth quarter, C.J. Stroud scored 20.9 on the bench, and Dak Prescott scored 12.6 in the lineup. The Cartel won by 17 anyway because everything else hit. Isaiah Likely, the tight end Sam cut a week ago, scored 26.9, George Pickens finally paid back some of his $22 keeper price with 23.5, and the Texans defense put up 15, the second-best number in the league. Mike D. has the easiest remaining schedule in the league and the deepest quarterback room in the sport. If he ever starts the right one, this is the best team in Fadunkadunk.

teams.name: Papas McButt Nuggets

nameHistory.name: Why dont you just call them?

teams.commentary: Other Mommy topped the box office this weekend, and Jordan's other quarterback topped his roster from the bench. He picked up Jordan Love, the one Brett A. cut, and left him on the bench to throw for 367 yards against Chicago and score 25.2 while Bo Nix scored 7.8. Rhamondre Stevenson scored 16 on the bench too, behind Carnell Tate's 1.1 in the flex. Jordan won anyway, by 4.4, with the seventh-best score of the week, because his kicker, Jason Myers, Frum's castoff, scored 23. That's nearly double what his two starting running backs scored combined, which is not the kind of stat a first-place team should own, and the committee dropped him to third. Oklahoma beat Texas with a kick on Saturday; Jordan beat Sam with one on Sunday. Jordan has now left 114 points on his bench this season, the most in the league by a distance. With Stefon Diggs out and Jordyn Tyson on IR, the receiver behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Garrett Wilson projects under 6 a game, and Jordan has spare backs to sell.

teams.name: Ammonia Coladas
teams.commentary: High Horse Rides Again was once this team's name, and the horse is officially back in the barn with a ribbon on it. Three weeks ago Mark lost to every team in the all-play. In the two weeks since, he has beaten every team in it both times, and he now leads the league in points. Lamar Jackson sat, so Drake Maye started and went for 39.3, the biggest overperformance of the week, while Bucky Irving went for 30.5, Malik Nabers 23.6 and Mike Evans 22.8 out of the flex. The 61-point beating of Frum was a formality. And this time he didn't leave anything behind: 2.1 bench points, after 26 a week ago. The weak spot is running back, where Kyle Monangai is out, Josh Jacobs is still parked on IR, and the next healthy option projects around 4 a game, but Evans gives Mark a spare receiver to deal for help.

teams.name: Captain Casper's Low Risk Tacos

nameHistory.name: Coach Matty Ps D In Swishs V

teams.commentary: The reigning champ climbed three spots with the second-best score of the week, a 40-point beating of Danny, and a lineup that finally looked like it was set on purpose. Jaylen Warren went for 33.8, Josh Allen scored 30.5 in Buffalo's overtime win over the Rams, Kyle Pitts filled in for a Travis Kelce on bye with 12.7, and Ka'imi Fairbairn kicked in 17. Brett also picked up the Jets defense and got 18, the best defensive score in any lineup in the league. It would have been a perfect move if the 49ers defense hadn't scored 20 on his bench on the same afternoon San Francisco moved to 5-0. Saquon Barkley is out and has 21 points in five weeks, so the backfield is Warren, Aaron Jones and RJ Harvey, who contributed 0.7 in the flex. The receiver room is thinner still with DeVonta Smith out, and Keenan Allen, Hearn's castoff, is now the next man up.

teams.name: $200 Dolla Holla
teams.commentary: Hearn owns the best all-play record in the league, a 36-19 mark that says he should be leading this thing, and he is 2-3 because the schedule keeps handing him the hottest team in the room. This week he scored 122.7, fifth-best in the league, and lost to the third-best by 17. Christian Watson went for 29.3 and James Cook for 22.3, but Deebo Samuel scored 1.5 before leaving early while Emeka Egbuka scored 14.2 on the bench. Hearn also cut the Packers defense a week after it scored 10, picked up the Bengals and got 9, and cut Keenan Allen, who scored 7 for Brett A. With A.J. Brown and Alec Pierce on IR and Deebo now out, the receiver depth is thin, and the next healthy option projects under 5 a game. The luck number says he's due. The roster says he should probably make a trade before the luck arrives.

teams.name: Christopher Dootron
teams.commentary: Sam set a perfect lineup this week. Every starter was the right call, zero points left on the bench, and he lost by 4.4 to a team that left nearly 40 on its own. If you want a one-sentence summary of fantasy football, that's it. Parker Washington, the $10 keeper who scored 1.5 a week ago, went for 27.4; Will Reichard, the kicker Sam picked up, scored 16; and Kirk Cousins, also picked up, started over Tyler Shough and scored 13.6 while Shough went negative on the bench. Pitbull released his 13th studio album this week, and Sam's pickup count for the season is already past that, with 18; for once, every one of this week's was a hit. Bijan was held to 13.8 and Omarion Hampton to 4.4, though, and with Jordan Mason on IR, the only back behind them projects for basically nothing. Sam has receivers to spare and still not enough running backs, and the waiver wire stopped being the answer a month ago.

teams.name: Table Shepherds McPie

nameHistory.name: your son rip  on line toot
Fernet and The Music Hall Mack

teams.commentary: The Table Shepherds lost by 36 with the eleventh-best score of the week and fell four spots to eighth, the biggest drop on the board. David Montgomery carried a doubtful tag into the lineup and scored 1.1 while Blake Corum scored 14.7 on the bench, DK Metcalf managed 3.8, and Daniel Carlson, the kicker Foy picked up to replace Harrison Mevis, scored 1. Jared Goff went for 28.9 in a comfortable Lions win, which only made the rest look worse. The defense carousel continues to spin: Foy picked up the Commanders, started them, and got 3 on the day Washington blew a 14-point fourth-quarter lead. He also grabbed Courtland Sutton after Danny cut him, and Sutton scored 8.8 on the bench. With Montgomery doubtful and Jonah Coleman on IR, the back behind Kyren Williams projects around 4 a game, and the second-hardest remaining schedule in the league is not going to wait.

teams.name: Los Desperados Sudados
teams.commentary: Danny finally set his lineup right, 1.6 points left on the bench after weeks of leaving a buffet back there, and the roster responded by scoring 103.8 and losing by 40. CeeDee Lamb, who scored 32.8 last week, played through a questionable tag for 1.9; Chase Brown scored 5.5; Ashton Jeanty managed 9.2. The one call that worked was on defense: he started the Broncos, who scored 14 on the day the Chargers fell to 0-5, and benched the Bears, who went negative while Jordan Love threw for 367 yards against them. Danny also cut Courtland Sutton, who scored 8.8 on Foy's bench. He is 1-4 with a winning all-play record and the worst luck number in the league, which makes him the league's most qualified expert on being robbed. The running back depth is still Rachaad White, at under 5 a game, behind two starters who just combined for 15.

teams.name: For Heaven Sakes, Woman
teams.commentary: UCLA went into Eugene and upset Oregon on Saturday, and on Sunday the league's 11th-ranked team beat the 10th, a smaller upset but Hess will take it. He did it with negative points from two different defenses, which is a genuine achievement. Hess picked up the Cowboys, projected second-best of the week, started them, and got negative 2; the Rams on his bench scored negative 1, so the decision didn't cost him, it just looked terrible. Puka Nacua went for 29.2 and Matthew Stafford for 27.2 in an overtime loss to the Bills, and Brenton Strange, a fresh pickup, gave him 10.3 at tight end. The other pickup, KC Concepcion, started in the flex and scored 1. Hess also cut four running backs in one week, so the depth chart behind Christian McCaffrey and TreVeyon Henderson is now Will Shipley, who is doubtful. That isn't depth, it's a wish, and he plays Mike D. next with the third-hardest schedule in the league ahead.

teams.name: Quintosss... Amigo?
teams.commentary: The Chiefs and Panthers both had byes this week, which took Patrick Mahomes, Tetairoa McMillan, Rashee Rice and Harrison Butker off Jeff's roster in one stroke, and the result was the lowest score of the week and a perfect 0-11 all-play. To replace Butker, Jeff picked up Harrison Mevis, the kicker Foy cut after three straight weeks of 3 points or fewer, and Mevis delivered exactly 3, a man of his word. In fairness, there was nothing left to do: Jeff left 0.1 points on the bench, the bench being mostly players on bye. Braelon Allen scored 18.1 and Brock Bowers 19, and the rest of the lineup, Quinshon Judkins at 6.5 and Tony Pollard at 5.2, did nothing to help. Breece Hall is out and Tank Bigsby is on IR, so the back behind Judkins and Pollard projects under 6 a game. The Amigos get Baker next, and the first-place team is not taking a bye.

teams.name: Dad Bellies Doin' Salt Smellies

nameHistory.name: Lots of ??? But Tons of Upside!
Poopy Wake Up Call On Line Toot
The Best Butt of the Bunch

teams.commentary: Frum made the move of the week and lost by 61 anyway, which is a very Dad Bellies way to spend a Sunday. With Bryce Young and Kenneth Walker on bye, he picked up Jacoby Brissett and started him for 24.7, and the new kicker, Spencer Shrader, kicked in 21. The kicker he cut to make room, Jason Myers, scored 23 for Jordan, so the kicker swap was a wash, but the quarterback move was a genuine save. Then Mark scored 159 and none of it mattered. Colston Loveland scored 2.9, Jaylen Waddle 3.8, and the Steelers defense 1. Frum has the hardest remaining schedule in the league and a backup receiver who projects under 4 a game, but Ollie Gordon II is a spare running back who just scored 14.8, and that's a trade chip. The Bellies are 1-4. The bellies, sadly, are not the problem.

commentary.intro: Bye weeks arrived on Sunday, the Chiefs and Panthers took the weekend off, and Fadunkadunk found out who had a plan B. Baker did: with Chuba Hubbard on a bye, the backup he finally bothered to pick up started and scored 16, and the Dino Nuggets take over first place. Jordan is still 4-1, but he won by less than five with the seventh-best score and nearly 40 points on his bench, and the committee has stopped mistaking survival for dominance. The real story is Mark. Three weeks ago the Coladas lost to every team in the all-play; for two straight weeks now they have beaten every team in it, and they've passed everybody in total points. Elsewhere, Mike D. owned three quarterbacks who scored 12.6, 20.9 and 32.1 and started the 12.6, Sam set a perfect lineup and lost anyway, and Hess somehow got negative points out of two different defenses.

awards.questionableStart: Mike D. had three healthy quarterbacks score 32.1, 20.9 and 12.6, and he started the 12.6. He won anyway, which only encourages him.
awards.closest: Jordan over Sam by 4.4. Sam left zero points on his bench, a perfect lineup; Jordan left nearly 40 on his. That's the sport.
awards.worstDefense: Hess picked up the Cowboys, the second-highest projected defense of the week, and got negative 2. The Rams on his bench scored negative 1, so at least the decision didn't matter.
awards.highScore: Mark, 159, his second straight perfect 11-0 week in the all-play.
awards.blowout: Mark over Frum by 60.8. Frum picked up a quarterback for the bye week and it still wasn't close.
awards.boom: Drake Maye, projected 18.4, scored 39.3 for Mark the week Lamar Jackson sat.
awards.bust: CeeDee Lamb, projected 15.5, scored 1.9 for Danny one week after scoring 32.8 for him.
awards.bestDefense: Brett A. picked up the Jets and got 18, the best defensive score in any lineup, while the 49ers scored 20 on his bench.
awards.luckiestWin: Jordan won with the seventh-best score of the week, by 4.4, with 39.7 on the bench.
awards.toughestLoss: Hearn scored 122.7, fifth-best in the league, and lost to the third-best.
awards.benchBomb: Mike D. benched Jayden Daniels (32.1) for Dak Prescott (12.6), a 19.5-point swing he survived.

commentary.outro:
Week 6 headliner: Jordan against Mark, third against fourth, the luckiest team in the league against the hottest one. Jordan is 4-1 and just left nearly 40 points on his bench; Mark has beaten every team in the league two weeks running. Baker gets Jeff, who will have his Chiefs and Panthers back and has to hope that's enough to slow down the first-place team. Mike D. gets Hess, Brett A. gets Frum, Hearn gets Foy, and Sam gets Danny in a meeting of the league's most cursed lineups.

Trade Desk: running backs are still the currency, and the bank keeps getting robbed. Sam has nothing behind Bijan and Hampton, Hess has a doubtful Will Shipley, Baker's backup projects around 2 a game, Brett A. lost Saquon, and Foy is one Montgomery tag away from starting Jacory Croskey-Merritt. The obvious deal is in Week 6's headline game: Jordan needs a receiver with Stefon Diggs out and has Rhamondre Stevenson, who just scored 16 on his bench; Mark needs a back with Kyle Monangai out and has Mike Evans, who just scored 22.8. Stevenson for Evans makes both teams better before they play each other. Frum's Ollie Gordon II is the other back on the market, and Sam has receivers to pay for him. Move of the week: Frum picking up Jacoby Brissett for a bye week and getting 24.7. Anti-move of the week: Jordan picking up Jordan Love and leaving him on the bench to score 25.2 while Bo Nix scored 7.8.

Swish Watch: the reigning champ is 3-2 and fifth, up three spots after the second-best score of the week. The Tacos keep winning without their most expensive running back, which is lucky, because Saquon Barkley has 21 points in five weeks and is now out. Luck Index: Jordan is the luckiest team in the league, 4-1 with a 28-27 all-play record; Danny is the unluckiest, 1-4 with a 31-24 all-play; and Hearn, 2-3 with the best all-play in the league, is a close second. Somebody check on Danny and Hearn. Rankings and commentary refresh every Tuesday morning once ESPN finalizes the week.
